You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited background contain court-context evidence, such as basketball-court lines on the playing surface or basketball equipment situated in a recognizable court setting?
node.criteria: Pass if visible court lines/surface or equipment in a recognizable court setting supports a basketball-court background; fail if assessable evidence consists only of isolated props or generic markings without court context; unknown if the relevant background cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Inspect the edited background and the relation of markings and equipment to the playing surface. This is evidence about the background, not a completion judgment; do not treat generic seams or isolated props as decisive.

node_traces.evidence: The edited background shows a basketball hoop and balls alongside visible court lines on a playing surface, providing recognizable basketball-court context.
The edited background shows a basketball hoop and balls alongside visible court lines on a playing surface, providing recognizable basketball-court context.
The edited background shows a basketball hoop and basketballs above a playing surface with visible court lines, providing recognizable basketball-court context.
The edited background shows a basketball hoop and basketballs in a recognizable court setting, with court lines visible on the playing surface.
The edited background shows a basketball hoop and basketballs, with court lines visible across the playing surface, supporting a recognizable basketball-court setting.

fulfillment: The binding is malformed and underspecified: “visibly (...) the background changed” leaves the decision target unclear, and the current wording can make a hoop/balls or a single floor line seem sufficient. Make the node explicitly assess the *background change relative to the source* and distinguish a recognizable playing area (e.g., coherent court surface/markings and basketball context) from basketball props against a dark or generic backdrop. Preserve partial progress for basketball-related edits that do not establish a court, and reserve unknown for genuinely unresolved visual evidence. The edited image visibly has a hoop, balls, and a light floor with a line, while support reports disagree about whether those cues form a recognizable court; do not resolve that disagreement by simply privileging one report or treating disagreement itself as failure. Instead make the criterion and evidence aggregation explicit and consistent, so repeated runs assess the same visual threshold. No transport, schema, or dependency failures are indicated; the variation is semantic/criterion ambiguity, not missing execution.
